stem:
Choose the word that correctly completes the sentence.

The two drivers ___ ready to leave.
hints: Look at the subject. Is it one person or more than one?
Find the subject: the two drivers. Count them.
A subject that means one takes a singular verb. A subject that means two or more takes a plural verb. Am goes only with I. Decide how many drivers there are, then pick the matching verb.

solution.methodName: Count the subject, then match the verb

steps.why: Ask: who is ready to leave? The drivers. The subject is who or what the sentence is about.

steps.action: Count the subject: "two drivers" means more than one, so the subject is plural.
steps.why: Plural means more than one. The word "two" and the -s at the end of "drivers" both tell you this.

steps.action: Match the verb: a plural subject takes "are".
steps.why: "is" goes with one person or thing. "are" goes with two or more. "am" goes only with I.

steps.action: Read it back: "The two drivers are ready to leave."
steps.why: Reading the full sentence is a quick check that the subject and verb match.

trapNotes.am: Am goes only with I, as in "I am ready."
trapNotes.is: Is goes with one person or thing, as in "The driver is ready." Here there are two drivers.
trapNotes.be: Be cannot follow the subject by itself here. It needs a helper word, as in "will be ready."
